engine: markdown
title: "rush convert"
---

```{term}
#| include: false
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
```

The `convert` command converts between formats without writing an expression.
It reads the input, infers the output format from the file extension (or `-O`),
and writes the result.

## Usage

```bash
rush convert [options] [<file>...]
```

## Basic conversion

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.parquet mtcars.csv
rush run 'nrow(df)' mtcars.parquet
```

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.json --head 3 mtcars.csv
cat mtcars.json
```

```{term}
rush convert -O jsonl --head 2 -o mtcars.jsonl mtcars.csv
cat mtcars.jsonl
```

## Output templates

Convert multiple files using an output template with yt-dlp-style placeholders:

```{term}
echo "id,val
1,a
2,b" > chunk1.csv
echo "id,val
3,c
4,d" > chunk2.csv
rush convert -o '%(file_name)s.parquet' chunk1.csv chunk2.csv
rush run 'df' chunk1.parquet
```

### Available placeholders

| Placeholder | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| `%(file_name)s` | Input file stem |
| `%(file_index)d` | 1-based file position |
| `%(table_name)s` | Table name (databases) |
| `%(table_index)d` | 1-based table position |

The format spec after `)` follows `sprintf()` conventions: `s` for string, `d`
for integer, `03d` for zero-padded. Use `l` for lowercase or `u` for uppercase:

```bash
rush convert -o '%(table_name)l.csv' sales.duckdb
rush convert -o 'table_%(table_index)03d.csv' big.duckdb
```

## Database output

When the output is a database format (DuckDB or SQLite), multiple inputs become
separate tables named after the input file stems:

```{term}
echo "id,val
1,a
2,b" > a.csv
echo "id,val
3,c
4,d" > b.csv
rush convert -o combined.duckdb a.csv b.csv
rush run 'names(dfs$combined)' combined.duckdb
```

A single input also uses the file name as the table name:

```{term}
rush convert -o cars_db.duckdb mtcars.csv
rush sql "SELECT cyl, COUNT(*) AS n FROM cars_db.mtcars GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY cyl" cars_db.duckdb
rm -f cars_db.duckdb
```

Convert between database formats:

```{term}
rush convert -o cars.duckdb mtcars.csv
rush convert -o copy.sqlite cars.duckdb
rush run 'names(dfs$copy)' copy.sqlite
```

## Limiting rows

Use `--head` to limit the number of rows written:

```{term}
rush convert --head 5 -o top5.csv mtcars.csv
cat top5.csv
```

## Format overrides

Force input and output formats regardless of extension with `-F` and `-O`:

```{term}
cp mtcars.csv mtcars.dat
rush convert -F csv -O json -o result.json --head 2 mtcars.dat
cat result.json
rm -f mtcars.dat
```

## Delimiter control

Override the output delimiter:

```{term}
rush convert -D ";" --head 3 -o mtcars_semi.csv mtcars.csv
cat mtcars_semi.csv
```

## XML element names

Use `--output-root` and `--output-record` to customize the XML structure:

```{term}
rush convert --output-root garage --output-record car --head 2 -o mtcars.xml mtcars.csv
cat mtcars.xml
rm -f mtcars.xml
```

## Help

```{term}
rush convert -h
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.parquet mtcars.json mtcars.jsonl chunk1.csv chunk2.csv chunk1.parquet chunk2.parquet
rm -f a.csv b.csv combined.duckdb cars.duckdb copy.sqlite
rm -f top5.csv result.json mtcars_semi.csv mtcars.dat
```
